newsitem.title: UK: Meyer down after cautious statement.
newsitem.headline: Meyer down after cautious statement.

text.p: Shares in Meyer International Plc fell on Wednesday after the builders' merchant group posted flat first-half profits coupled with a cautious statement on the outlook for the rest of the year.
The stock was down 20p at 367-1/2 by 1127 GMT -- its lowest since early August -- in volume of over 370,000 shares .
Chairman Harry Langman said demand was still below last year's levels though there were signs of an improvement in the outlook in its key markets.
He said softwood prices continued to recover and the improvement in housing starts and transactions should lead to increased demand for timber and building materials.

Langman said it was "...unlikely that these better conditions will impact on the group's results until next year" though the "actions taken by the group over the last twelve months to improve the performance of our key businesses...will allow us to take advantage of any upswing in demand."
Meyer's pretax profit rose slightly to 20.3 million stg in the first half to September 30, from 20.1 million, and the dividend was unchanged at 4.2p.
Turnover dipped to 599.4 million stg from 638.4 million.
